label: Levied by
value: Local governments (counties, cities, school districts and other taxing jurisdictions) set mill levies on state-certified taxable values
note: Total mills from all jurisdictions are applied to the property's taxable value.
source_title: Montana Department of Revenue: Certified Property Values and Mill Levies

label: State oversight
value: Montana Department of Revenue, Property Assessment Division
note: The State itself values taxable property statewide and certifies taxable values to local governments.
source_title: Montana Department of Revenue: Property Assessment Division

label: Local levy growth limit
value: Property tax revenue may grow by one-half of the average inflation rate over the past three years (plus newly taxable property)
note: Sets each jurisdiction's maximum mills under MCA 15-10-420.
source_title: Montana Department of Revenue: Certified Property Values and Mill Levies

label: Residential tax rates for primary homes and long-term rentals (2026)
value: Tiered: 0.76% on the first $378,000 of market value, 0.90% to $756,000, 1.10% to $1,511,999, 1.90% above; flat 1.90% for other residential property
note: New state rate structure from 2026 that favours primary residences and long-term rentals over second homes and short-term rentals.
source_title: Montana Department of Revenue: 2026 Property Tax Information

label: Real estate transfer tax
value: None: the Montana Constitution prohibits the State and local governments from taxing the sale or transfer of real property
note: Article VIII, Section 17, approved by voters on November 2, 2010 (Constitutional Initiative 105).
source_title: Montana Legislature: Montana Constitution, Article VIII, Section 17
